is_anopheles.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected as larvae from five counties in Kenya and identified as Anopheles gambiae s.l. (An. coluzzii, An. gambiae, An. arabiensis, An. quadriannulatus) via whole genome sequencing (WGS). Page 3, Methods.

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports amino acid substitution frequencies for target-site resistance markers in Vgsc (L995F, V402L, I1527T, N1570Y, P1874L/S), Ace-1 (G280S), and Rdl (A296G/S). Page 8, Figure 4a and Supplementary Figures S4/S5.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Figure 4a presents exact allele frequencies for Vgsc variants (L995F 62%, V402L 38%, I1527T 38%, N1570Y 10%) in Kenya Turkana 2019 An. coluzzii, with sample sizes specified in Table 1 (N = 21 An. coluzzii in 2019). Page 4 Table 1 & Page 8 Figure 4a.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected as larvae from breeding sites in five counties in Kenya (Busia, Kwale, Turkana, Kirinyaga, Kiambu) between 2006 and 2021 and reared to adults. Page 3, Methods.

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study reporting novel whole genome sequencing and marker frequency analysis of field-collected Anopheles mosquitoes in Kenya.

sub_country_location.evidence: Sampling sites are specified at high spatial resolution with coordinates in Table 1: Teso in Busia, Kwale in Kwale, Kakuma in Turkana (3.717 N, 34.857 E), Mwea in Kirinyaga, and Thika in Kiambu. Page 4, Table 1.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Sampling times are recorded by year and month (e.g., Turkana 2006 month 2, 2019 month 1, and 2019 month 9). Figure 4a reports marker frequencies specifically for 2019. Page 4 Table 1 & Page 8 Figure 4.

duplicate_risk.evidence: Some archived samples from earlier years (2006-2014) were combined with new 2019-2021 collections, but the WGS dataset and marker frequency analyses are newly generated for this study (ENA accessions ERR11811571-ERR11811786 etc.). Page 3 & Page 10.

supplement.evidence: Target-site resistance marker frequencies for Vgsc L995F, V402L, I1527T, and N1570Y are fully displayed in Figure 4a of the main text.

assessment.summary: This primary study collected Anopheles gambiae s.l. larvae across five counties in Kenya (2006-2021) and performed whole genome sequencing on 564 quality-filtered specimens. It reports the first discovery of Anopheles coluzzii in Kenya (Turkana County) and provides extractable allele frequencies for target-site resistance markers in An. coluzzii from 2019, including Vgsc L995F (62%), V402L (38%), I1527T (38%), and N1570Y (10%).
